q: In the diameter solution, what does the recursive function return?
why: The parent can only extend a straight path through the child, so it needs the height.

q: isBalanced that calls a separate height() at every node costs, on a skewed tree…
why: height() is O(n) and it's called for n nodes. Returning height with a −1 failure signal makes it O(n).

q: In the LCA recursion, a node receives non-null results from BOTH children. Meaning?
options: p and q are in different subtrees, so this node is the LCA
Both are in the left subtree
why: This is the split point: the lowest node with p on one side and q on the other.

q: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum: why take max(gain(child), 0)?
options: A branch with a negative sum only lowers the total, so skip it
why: It's always allowed to not extend into a subtree.

q: Count Good Nodes (no bigger value on the path from the root): what goes into the recursion?
options: The node and the maximum value seen on the path so far
why: A condition that depends on ancestors is passed down as a parameter.
